paper_metadata.title: Extent of Medial Temporal Resection on Outcome from Anterior Temporal Lobectomy: A Randomized Prospective Study Operative Technique

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a well-defined, homogeneous sample with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria. Recruitment was consecutive among eligible patients with a high participation rate (93%), and baseline characteristics were thoroughly described and balanced between groups.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Patients who met the following criteria were considered eligible for randomization in this study: 1) medically intractable seizures; 2) nonretarded (Wechsler adult intelligence scale-revised full-scale intelligence quotient, >69); 3) chronological age between 18 and 40 years; 4) no magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) evidence of foreign tissue lesions; and 5) at least three seizures of unilateral mesial temporal lobe origin
items.reasoning: The authors provide specific clinical, cognitive, and age-based parameters defining the target population.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Patients meeting these criteria were informed of their eligibility for study participation at the end of long-term monitoring with strip electrodes.
items.reasoning: The recruitment process is linked to a specific clinical workflow (post-monitoring) at identified epilepsy centers.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: All of the patients underwent ATL under general anesthesia between January 1990 and August 1992.
items.reasoning: The specific start and end dates for the surgical recruitment are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Epilepsy Center (ARW), Swedish Medical Center, Seattle, Washington; Epi-Care Center (BPH), Baptist Memorial Hospital, Memphis, Tennessee
items.reasoning: The specific medical centers and cities are listed in the author affiliations and methods.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Patients who met the following criteria were considered eligible for randomization in this study: 1) medically intractable seizures; 2) nonretarded... 3) chronological age between 18 and 40 years; 4) no magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) evidence of foreign tissue lesions; and 5) at least three seizures of unilateral mesial temporal lobe origin
items.reasoning: Detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria are provided, including the 'zero time' (post-monitoring/pre-surgery).

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Of the eligible candidates, five declined to participate.
items.reasoning: With 70 patients randomized and only 5 declining, the participation rate is approximately 93%, which is well above the 80% threshold for low risk.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: As shown in Table 1, there were no differences between the partial and total hippocampectomy groups in terms of the following variables: chronological age (P=0.40), age at onset of epilepsy (Table I) (P=0.10), gender (P=0.64), laterality of surgery (P=0.67), speech lateralization (left, right, bilateral) (P=0.38), presence/absence of hippocampal sclerosis
items.reasoning: Table 1 and the text provide a comprehensive breakdown of demographics and clinical baseline data.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study reports 100% follow-up for the primary 1-year seizure outcome. While some pathology data was missing for a subset in the regression, the primary analysis included the full randomized cohort.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: The partial and total hippocampectomy groups had minimum follow-ups of 1 year... At 1-year follow-up, there was a significant effect of type of surgery (χ2 [1] = 6.86, P = 0.009).
items.reasoning: The analysis accounts for all 70 randomized patients at the 1-year mark.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: Because there was no significant dropout for the primary outcome, the authors did not need to describe retrieval methods for lost participants.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: This analysis included 61 patients, because pathology specimens were unobtainable for 9 patients.
items.reasoning: The authors explain why a subset was excluded from the specific regression analysis (missing pathology), though they were included in the main outcome analysis.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The text does not explicitly compare the 9 patients with missing pathology to the rest of the cohort, though they were not 'lost to follow-up' for the seizure outcome itself.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: The above analysis was recalculated, deleting the hippocampal sclerosis variable so that all 70 patients could be included. Again, only the extent of resection was statistically significant
items.reasoning: The authors performed sensitivity analysis including the full cohort to ensure the missing pathology data did not bias the results.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (extent of resection) was a randomized intervention, which is the highest level of control. The surgical technique was standardized and the measurement of the 'dose' (resection length) was anatomically defined.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: In one group, hippocampus was resected only to the level of the anterior margin of the cerebral peduncle. In the other, hippocampus was removed more posteriorly, to the level of the superior colliculus.
items.reasoning: The 'dose' of the prognostic factor (resection extent) is clearly defined by anatomical landmarks.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: The entire dissection of hippocampus was performed using the operating microscope... By placing these single and double silver clips on the anterior and posterior edges, the specimen could be aligned after fixation
items.reasoning: The use of microscopic surgery and silver clip marking provides a reliable method for ensuring the intended resection extent was achieved.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: randomized to one of two types of surgery (described below).
items.reasoning: The PF is categorical (Partial vs Total) based on the randomized design, not a post-hoc cut-point.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All of the patients underwent ATL under general anesthesia between January 1990 and August 1992. The surgery did not vary between dominant and nondominant hemispheres.
items.reasoning: The surgical setting and general approach were standardized for all participants.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: randomized to one of two surgical groups. At ATL, both groups had equal amounts of lateral temporal cortex excised. The only difference between groups was the degree of hippocampal resection.
items.reasoning: PF data is complete for all 70 patients as it was the assigned intervention.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: No PF data was missing, so imputation was not required.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure freedom) was assessed by personnel blinded to the surgical group, using a very strict definition (zero seizures/auras). Multiple independent verifications were performed.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Seizure-free patients experienced absolutely no seizures (including auras) after surgery. Patients experiencing simple partial seizures (auras), complex partial seizures, or generalized seizures were rated as not seizure-free.
items.reasoning: The definition is exceptionally clear and rigorous, including the exclusion of auras from the 'seizure-free' category.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: seizure outcome was judged by blinded personnel and not by the unblinded surgeon... two different project staff members (research nurse, neuropsychology fellow) blinded to type of surgery, independently contacted the patients
items.reasoning: Blinding of outcome assessors and independent double-verification are strong safeguards against measurement bias.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The patients were typically seen by blinded study personnel for routine follow-up at 1, 3, 6, 9, and 12 months and yearly thereafter
items.reasoning: The follow-up schedule and assessment methods were uniform across both groups.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Outcome Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Outcome of interest is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: As a randomized trial, confounding is inherently controlled. The authors also verified the balance of key confounders (age, onset, pathology) and used multivariable logistic regression to further adjust for these factors.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: chronological age, age at onset of epilepsy, gender, laterality of surgery, speech lateralization... presence/absence of hippocampal sclerosis
items.reasoning: The study identifies and measures the primary known prognostic factors in epilepsy surgery.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: The hippocampal pathology grading system was based on reviewing serial sections of hippocampus removed en bloc... Grade 1: mild... Grade 4: marked
items.reasoning: Confounders like pathology are not just noted but graded using a specific, published system.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: The presence of layers in continuity provides a direct measure of how posterior the hippocampal resection went... pathology specimens were reviewed
items.reasoning: Pathological grading and clinical history are standard and reliable measures in this context.

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The randomization process was clearly successful in equating groups in terms of potential confounding variables.
items.reasoning: Baseline measurements were taken using the same protocols for all patients during the pre-surgical evaluation.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods are used if imputation is used for missing confounder data.
items.evidence_snippet: This analysis included 61 patients, because pathology specimens were unobtainable for 9 patients. The above analysis was recalculated, deleting the hippocampal sclerosis variable so that all 70 patients could be included.
items.reasoning: The authors used complete case analysis but validated it with a sensitivity analysis of the full cohort, which is an appropriate way to handle the small amount of missing confounder data.

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: randomized to one of two types of surgery... The randomization process was clearly successful in equating groups
items.reasoning: Randomization is the gold standard for accounting for both known and unknown confounders in the study design.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: A logistic regression analysis was computed... Independent variables included extent of resection, age at surgery, age at onset of epilepsy, laterality of surgery, gender, and presence/absence of hippocampal sclerosis.
items.reasoning: Multivariable adjustment was performed to confirm the independent effect of the PF.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Confounding Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Important potential confounders are appropriately accounted for, limiting potential bias with respect to the relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical approach is robust, utilizing Chi-square for primary proportions, Logistic Regression for adjustment, and Survival Analysis (Log-rank) for longitudinal data. Results are reported transparently for all outcomes.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: The preoperative minus postoperative difference score was computed for each index and subjected to analysis of variance... logistic regression analysis was computed... survival analyses were calculated for time to first seizure.
items.reasoning: The authors clearly outline the statistical tests used for each type of data (seizure, memory, and time-to-event).

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: The degree of hippocampal sclerosis was included as a predictor variable, because we had previously found it to be a significant predictor of memory outcome after ATL (20).
items.reasoning: Variable selection was based on prior clinical evidence and established prognostic factors.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: examination of time to first seizure (survival analysis) revealed significantly superior outcomes associated with total hippocampectomy.
items.reasoning: Survival analysis is the most appropriate method for longitudinal seizure data to account for varying follow-up times and the timing of events.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: Material-specific memory effects after left or right ATL were examined (Table 3). For patients undergoing right ATL, there were no significant findings for any memory measure.
items.reasoning: The authors report both significant and non-significant results across all pre-specified domains (seizure and neuropsychological).

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Statistical Analysis and Presentation Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: The statistical analysis is appropriate for the design of the study, limiting potential for presentation of invalid or spurious results.
